puc_mapping.tryPush+pushResolved: luaT_callTMres stages func+p1+p2 at L->top (ltm.c:119-131); no intermediate callable-resolution layer because PUC metamethods are called as plain values through luaD_call
puc_mapping.pushBytecodeExecFrame: luaD_precall LUA_VLCL branch (ldo.c:725-735): narg derived from L->top - func - 1; checkstackp; prepCallInfo; nil-fill missing params
puc_mapping.prepareHostArgs: has NO PUC counterpart as a separate decision — PUC's luaT_callTMres setobj2s writes ARE the staging; precall never classifies argument storage origin
puc_mapping.args_on_stack classification: NO PUC counterpart — PUC precall consumes (func slot, nresults) and derives narg from the stack top; the caller's staging decision is implicit in where it wrote the values

verifier_hypothesis_check.hypothesis: luazig activation decides argument STORAGE ORIGIN (pointer-test args.ptr == &bc_stack[func_slot+1]); PUC's precall never does that — callers stage on the stack first.
verifier_hypothesis_check.evidence: vm.zig:11329-11334 (args_on_stack blk) + vm.zig:11336-11345 (prepareHostArgs dispatch); measured cost of the classification + host-branch + call-setup on the metamethod path: (4.0+9.2)% of pushBytecodeExecFrame (11.77% global) = ~1.55% global, plus prepareHostArgs prologue/marshaling 2.11% global that a fused staging write would partially recover.
verifier_hypothesis_check.architectural_note: The pointer test is not merely a perf cost: it makes the activation ABI depend on WHERE the caller stored args, which is the opposite of PUC's contract (caller stages on stack; precall consumes slot+count). Category-A callers (OP_CALL) are already staged by construction; Category-B callers pay a classification that always answers 'host' and then copies — exactly what luaT_callTMres's setobj2s would do, but reached through a guessing layer.

t3_activation_abi_inventory.description: Every production call site of pushBytecodeExecFrame at HEAD 761df30, classified. A = func+args already contiguous in bc_stack (must stay zero-copy). B = logically a PUC stack-call (PUC stages func+args on the stack, then luaD_precall consumes slot+count) but luazig passes a host slice. C = genuine host boundary.

sites.note: Closest thing to a genuine host boundary (Category C): the args arrive from outside the VM. But the PUC-faithful contract still holds: staging them onto bc_stack before activation is exactly what the C API does in PUC.

abi_answer.question: Should the activation primitive consume a staged slot+count like PUC precall instead of args:[]const Value?
reasoning: Every Category-A site already has func+args contiguous in bc_stack and knows nargs locally — a staged slot+count ABI serves them with ZERO copy and removes the pointer classification entirely (they call the core activation directly with (func_slot, nargs)).

Every Category-B site is a PUC stack-call whose PUC implementation stages func+args on the stack first (luaT_callTMres/luaT_callTM/luaD_hook/luaB_pcall/luaG_errormsg). A shared staging primitive (stageBytecodeCall: reserve, write [func, args...], return {func_slot, nargs}) reproduces the PUC sequence exactly and is reusable by ALL B sites.

The only C-adjacent site (runBytecodeInternal, vm.zig:11991) is also stack-staged in PUC (the C API pushes args before lua_pcall), so it fits the same staging primitive — no separate host ABI is needed.

The args:[]const Value ABI forces the activation to GUESS storage origin (pointer test) — a decision PUC's precall never makes. The guess is pure overhead for A (always 'stack') and pure overhead for B (always 'host' -> copy through a noinline boundary with 6-arg marshaling measured at 37.5% of prepareHostArgs).
Transition safety: a thin compatibility wrapper (accepts args slice -> stages -> activates) keeps unmigrated B callers working while the measured metamethod path migrates first.

proposed_abi.stage: stageBytecodeCall(func_slot, callee_cl, args) -> StagedCall{func_slot, nargs} — PUC luaT_callTMres setobj2s sequence: ensure capacity for func+args, write callee at func_slot, copy args to func_slot+1..; bc_stack_top NOT bumped (activation owns the top update, preserving today's errdefer transactionality exactly).
proposed_abi.activate: pushStagedBytecodeExecFrame(exec_frames, proto, func_slot, nargs, callee_cl, nresults) — PUC luaD_precall LUA_VLCL: contract is 'func + nargs args already staged at func_slot'; derives everything from the stack; no pointer test, no host copy, no storage-origin classification.
proposed_abi.compat_wrapper: pushBytecodeExecFrame(exec_frames, proto, args, callee_cl, caller_func_slot, nresults) — during migration only: pointer-test (transitional) -> in-place activate (A) or stage+activate (B). Deleted once A sites call the core directly and B sites stage explicitly.
